competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
indicators: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.
Summarize the findings of simple analyses (e.g., descriptive statistics or basic trends) in a straightforward manner. Focus on clarity and conciseness.
Use basic visual tools (e.g., Excel charts, basic Python/R plotting) to represent data in ways that make trends and relationships easy to understand.
Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.
Cite sources of information/AI-generated content in visuals.

competencies.competency: Working Effectively with Others (Mobilize People; Collaborate with Partners and Stakeholders)
competencies.description: Working Effectively with Others is the ability to build strong, collaborative relationships within and outside the organization. It involves sharing information openly, encouraging diverse viewpoints, and enabling teamwork to solve problems and achieve shared goals. This competency extends to supporting others through change, providing constructive feedback, mobilizing teams around a common purpose, and fostering partnerships that amplify organizational effectiveness.
indicators: Share relevant information to facilitate collaboration.
Accomplish independent tasks as part of one's own share of the work.
Work with others to clearly define problems and identify suitable solutions.
Suggest methods and means for maximizing the input and involvement of team members.
Facilitate the expression of diverse points of view to enhance teamwork.
Openly share data/findings to support other teams' work.

competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
indicators: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.

Use basic visual tools (e.g., Excel charts, basic Python/R plotting) to represent data in ways that make trends and relationships easy to understand.
Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.
Cite sources of information/AI-generated content in visuals.

AI-human Collaborative Recommendation De.description:
September 30 is now recognized as a federal statutory day of commemoration. The day provides an opportunity to reflect on the tragic history of residential schools and honour their Survivors by engaging in reconciliation activities within our communities. 
Guest speakers share their thoughts and insights on what those experiences mean for Indigenous Peoples in Canada and for us all as we continue the journey towards truth and reconciliation.

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the commitment to ethical behavior, transparency, and fairness in all professional actions. This competency involves consistently adhering to organizational values, ethical guidelines, and legal standards especially when handling sensitive data or implementing analytical methods. It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
indicators: Comply with the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector in all aspects of data/AI use.
Discuss ethical concerns with appropriate individuals or channels and seek guidance for ethical/privacy issues.
Identify and report ethical concerns when appropriate.
Adhere to the organization's legal, privacy and ethical frameworks (Privacy Act, Policy on Privacy Protection, etc.) and follow disclosure procedures.
Identify and proactively flag privacy/security/accessibility implications.
Consult responsible AI resources.
Consult key policies/procedures on AI for decision-making.
Ensure privacy/security is set at the right permission levels.

indicators: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the commitment to ethical behavior, transparency, and fairness in all professional actions. This competency involves consistently adhering to organizational values, ethical guidelines, and legal standards especially when handling sensitive data or implementing analytical methods. It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
indicators: Comply with the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector in all aspects of data/AI use.
Discuss ethical concerns with appropriate individuals or channels and seek guidance for ethical/privacy issues.
Identify and report ethical concerns when appropriate.
Adhere to the organization's legal, privacy and ethical frameworks (Privacy Act, Policy on Privacy Protection, etc.) and follow disclosure procedures.
Identify and proactively flag privacy/security/accessibility implications.
Consult responsible AI resources.
Consult key policies/procedures on AI for decision-making.
Ensure privacy/security is set at the right permission levels.

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the commitment to ethical behavior, transparency, and fairness in all professional actions. This competency involves consistently adhering to organizational values, ethical guidelines, and legal standards especially when handling sensitive data or implementing analytical methods. It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
indicators: Comply with the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector in all aspects of data/AI use.
Discuss ethical concerns with appropriate individuals or channels and seek guidance for ethical/privacy issues.
Identify and report ethical concerns when appropriate.
Adhere to the organization's legal, privacy and ethical frameworks (Privacy Act, Policy on Privacy Protection, etc.) and follow disclosure procedures.
Identify and proactively flag privacy/security/accessibility implications.
Consult responsible AI resources.
Consult key policies/procedures on AI for decision-making.
Ensure privacy/security is set at the right permission levels.

competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
indicators: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.
Summarize the findings of simple analyses (e.g., descriptive statistics or basic trends) in a straightforward manner. Focus on clarity and conciseness.
Use basic visual tools (e.g., Excel charts, basic Python/R plotting) to represent data in ways that make trends and relationships easy to understand.
Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.
Cite sources of information/AI-generated content in visuals.

Set clear expectations, monitor progress, and address performance constructively.
Promote a shared sense of purpose and continuous learning through goal setting and development opportunities.
Implement strategies that strengthen collaboration and support a high-performance culture.

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the commitment to ethical behavior, transparency, and fairness in all professional actions. This competency involves consistently adhering to organizational values, ethical guidelines, and legal standards especially when handling sensitive data or implementing analytical methods. It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
indicators: Design and execute Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) and Algorithmic Impact Assessments (AIAs) for AI systems or processes.
Use AIA tool to assess/monitor automated decision risks.
Help others determine when/how to use AIA.
Evaluate the ethical, legal, and social implications of AI models before deployment.
Advise teams on mitigating risks such as bias, misinformation, and overreliance on AI-generated content.
Recommend inclusive design strategies that accommodate diverse user needs and reduce systemic bias.
Interpret and translate Treasury Board Secretariat (TBS) directives (e.g., Directive on Automated Decision-Making) into operational practices.
Ensure compliance with the Voluntary Code of Conduct on Generative AI and the FASTER principles
Mentor others in navigating complex ethical dilemmas in AI deployment and data use.
Provide guidance/advice on responsible data/AI tools (e.g., AIA).
Help colleagues apply accessibility and best practices for communication.
Consult authoritative data sources for alignment with data authority/intended use (e.g. Personal Information Bank (PIB) and PIA's, Digital Privacy Playbook, etc.)
Help and encourage colleagues to apply responsible AI guidance (peer-to-peer support via coaching, communities of practice, research publications, etc.)
Identify and remove barriers to data sharing.

indicators: Facilitate inclusive collaboration by encouraging diverse contributions and perspectives across teams and communities.
Coach and challenge others to build capability and confidence in complex decision-making.
Leverage team strengths and differences to achieve shared goals and foster innovation.
Model open communication by actively listening, giving honest feedback, and recognizing contributions.
Set clear expectations, monitor progress, and address performance constructively.
Promote a shared sense of purpose and continuous learning through goal setting and development opportunities.
Implement strategies that strengthen collaboration and support a high-performance culture.

competencies.description: The Artificial Intelligence Techniques competency encompasses the knowledge and skills required to develop, deploy, and manage AI-driven solutions, including machine learning algorithms, deep learning models, natural language processing (NLP), and generative AI systems. It covers the full AI pipeline from data preparation and model development to ethical considerations and model deployment.
indicators: Apply basic machine learning algorithms, including supervised and unsupervised techniques.
Define core AI concepts, such as machine learning, deep learning, large language models, and vision-language models.
Use open-source libraries to build basic models.
Perform effective prompt engineering.
Evaluate the quality of LLM's.

competencies.description: Data processing refers to the collection, cleaning, transformation, and manipulation of raw data into a format suitable for analysis and decision-making. It involves handling data from various sources, ensuring its quality, and making it ready for statistical analysis or machine learning models.
indicators: Load datasets from common formats (CSV, Excel, SQL) and perform basic cleaning tasks such as handling missing values and formatting issues.
Apply data transformations such as filtering, aggregating, and sorting to prepare data for analysis.
Derive variables to enhance data analysis.
Apply methods to handle missing data (e.g., drop missing records).
Describe the stages of the full data lifecycle (plan, collect, process, use, share, dispose).

competencies.competency: Thinking Things Through (Create Vision and Strategy)
competencies.description: Thinking Things Through is the ability to systematically analyze problems, identify patterns and connections, and develop well-informed plans and recommendations. This competency involves asking the right questions, evaluating cause and effect relationships, and turning analysis into clear strategies that align with organizational goals.
indicators: Inform analysis with a thorough understanding of the environment.
Translate implementation strategies, objectives and direction into concrete activities.
Contribute expertise and insight to the development and implementation of organizational strategies.
Communicate with clarity and conviction.
Respond to changes in direction and organizational priorities.
Design and implement solutions to operational challenges.

competencies.description: Knowledge and ability to design, define, construct, enhance, support, and maintain software associated with machine learning.
indicators: Write basic programs that include variables, loops, conditionals, and functions to perform simple data tasks.
Use basic data structures such as lists, arrays, and dictionaries to store and manipulate data.
Recognize and correct common programming errors, such as syntax and logical mistakes.
Manipulate data using built-in functions and libraries (e.g., Python's Pandas or R's dplyr).
Use at least one open-source programming language, typically Python or R, for basic data manipulation and analysis tasks.
Consider use of open source over commercial tools.

competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
indicators: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.
Summarize the findings of simple analyses (e.g., descriptive statistics or basic trends) in a straightforward manner. Focus on clarity and conciseness.
Use basic visual tools (e.g., Excel charts, basic Python/R plotting) to represent data in ways that make trends and relationships easy to understand.
Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.
Cite sources of information/AI-generated content in visuals.

competencies.competency: Showing Initiative and Being Action Oriented (Achieve Results; Promote Innovation and Guide Change)
competencies.description: Showing Initiative and Being Action Oriented is the ability to proactively accomplish tasks, adapt to shifting priorities, and effectively plan to achieve results even when faced with challenges. It includes anticipating and overcoming obstacles, driving projects forward, and using resourcefulness to both improve performance and promote innovation. This competency extends to encouraging experimentation and new ideas, demonstrating resilience amid change, and taking ownership for outcomes.
indicators: Align people with work to achieve organizational objectives and results
Monitor and control work unit resources
Set and revise operational plans to reflect changing priorities or conditions
Inform decision-making with sound understanding of context, data and evidence
Demonstrate and promote stewardship of financial and organizational resources
Make challenging decisions and take action at the opportune time
Take ownership and acknowledge impact and outcome of decisions
Encourage and apply sound risk management practices
Identify opportunities for and barriers to innovation
Propose creative practices, concepts or products
Encourage employees to generate new and innovative approaches
Adjust practices to address lessons learned following setbacks and mistakes
Adapt plans in response to changes in direction and priorities
Evaluate the impact of change on employees and take appropriate action
Demonstrate resilience, composure and a positive outlook in an environment of uncertainty and ambiguity

competencies.description: Business acumen in data science refers to the ability to understand and apply knowledge of business operations, strategy, and decision-making processes. It involves identifying business needs, aligning data-driven insights with organizational goals, and making decisions that drive organizational success.
indicators: Head the creation of data-driven business models that optimize profitability, revenue generation, or customer engagement. Ensure alignment with long-term business strategy.
Guide senior Leadership on strategic decisions based on data insights, providing recommendations that align with both short- and long-term business goals.
Champion the integration of data-driven decision-making across all business functions, promoting a culture of data-driven Leadership.
Manage cross-functional teams to ensure data-driven projects meet organizational goals and generate measurable business value.
Head innovation initiatives that leverage data science to transform business processes, create new revenue streams, or disrupt the market.
Help others translate organizational needs/mandate into data/AI requirements for projects.
Apply governance in specific operational business contexts (e.g., obtaining policy guideline approval).
Define and implement strategies for advancing organizational AI talent, systems, and infrastructure.

indicators: Implement branching and merging strategies in Git to manage collaborative codebases.

Document functions and scripts using standardized formats (e.g., Python docstrings) to ensure reproducibility.
Review and test AI-assisted code to ensure validity, relevance and adherence to GoC standards.

competencies.description: Knowledge in a range of mathematical and statistical techniques, understanding and being able to apply them, and comprehending their underlying assumptions and limitations.

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the commitment to ethical behavior, transparency, and fairness in all professional actions. This competency involves consistently adhering to organizational values, ethical guidelines, and legal standards especially when handling sensitive data or implementing analytical methods. It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
indicators: Design and execute Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) and Algorithmic Impact Assessments (AIAs) for AI systems or processes.
Use AIA tool to assess/monitor automated decision risks.
Help others determine when/how to use AIA.
Evaluate the ethical, legal, and social implications of AI models before deployment.
Advise teams on mitigating risks such as bias, misinformation, and overreliance on AI-generated content.
Recommend inclusive design strategies that accommodate diverse user needs and reduce systemic bias.

Ensure compliance with the Voluntary Code of Conduct on Generative AI and the FASTER principles
Mentor others in navigating complex ethical dilemmas in AI deployment and data use.
Provide guidance/advice on responsible data/AI tools (e.g., AIA).
Help colleagues apply accessibility and best practices for communication.
Consult authoritative data sources for alignment with data authority/intended use (e.g. Personal Information Bank (PIB) and PIA's, Digital Privacy Playbook, etc.)
Help and encourage colleagues to apply responsible AI guidance (peer-to-peer support via coaching, communities of practice, research publications, etc.)
Identify and remove barriers to data sharing.

indicators: Facilitate inclusive collaboration by encouraging diverse contributions and perspectives across teams and communities.
Coach and challenge others to build capability and confidence in complex decision-making.
Leverage team strengths and differences to achieve shared goals and foster innovation.
Model open communication by actively listening, giving honest feedback, and recognizing contributions.
Set clear expectations, monitor progress, and address performance constructively.
Promote a shared sense of purpose and continuous learning through goal setting and development opportunities.
Implement strategies that strengthen collaboration and support a high-performance culture.

competencies.competency: Working Effectively with Others (Mobilize People; Collaborate with Partners and Stakeholders)
competencies.description: Working Effectively with Others is the ability to build strong, collaborative relationships within and outside the organization. It involves sharing information openly, encouraging diverse viewpoints, and enabling teamwork to solve problems and achieve shared goals. This competency extends to supporting others through change, providing constructive feedback, mobilizing teams around a common purpose, and fostering partnerships that amplify organizational effectiveness.
indicators: Share relevant information to facilitate collaboration.
Accomplish independent tasks as part of one's own share of the work.
Work with others to clearly define problems and identify suitable solutions.
Suggest methods and means for maximizing the input and involvement of team members.
Facilitate the expression of diverse points of view to enhance teamwork.
Openly share data/findings to support other teams' work.

competencies.description: Knowledge and ability to design, define, construct, enhance, support, and maintain software associated with machine learning.
indicators: Write basic programs that include variables, loops, conditionals, and functions to perform simple data tasks.
Use basic data structures such as lists, arrays, and dictionaries to store and manipulate data.
Recognize and correct common programming errors, such as syntax and logical mistakes.
Manipulate data using built-in functions and libraries (e.g., Python's Pandas or R's dplyr).
Use at least one open-source programming language, typically Python or R, for basic data manipulation and analysis tasks.
Consider use of open source over commercial tools.

competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
indicators: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.
Summarize the findings of simple analyses (e.g., descriptive statistics or basic trends) in a straightforward manner. Focus on clarity and conciseness.
Use basic visual tools (e.g., Excel charts, basic Python/R plotting) to represent data in ways that make trends and relationships easy to understand.
Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.
Cite sources of information/AI-generated content in visuals.

competencies.description: Knowledge in a range of mathematical and statistical techniques, understanding and being able to apply them, and comprehending their underlying assumptions and limitations.

Consult key policies/procedures on AI for decision-making.
